column1: # Super Mario Odyssey on Android (keys in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md "Game profiles on Android")
# Nintendo EPD's sead / agl engine (NintendoWare G3d / Ui2d / Vfx) on SDK 7.3.2, update 1.4.1; 27,984 shaders, all translated. The upstream profile as it is.
# Tested 2026-10-30 on the Legion Y700 (TB322FC, Snapdragon 8 Elite, Adreno 830, Android 16), driven with DM_CTL: the controller notice, the title, a new save's opening (the airship,
# Bowser, the cap torn), Cap Kingdom from waking up (Look Around, the hills, the steps, the bridge) to Cappy's cutscene and "Cappy is now your companion", the cap throw, Bonneton's
# square; the game saved there and after a restart it continues with Cappy. HUD counters, the map, the pause menu's mode switch (docked 1600x900 / handheld 1280x720) checked.
# 60 fps in both modes: docked at the wake-up field 1,230 draws, replay 6.4 ms and GPU 8.8 ms a frame, Bonneton 1,050 draws, replay 6.5 ms and GPU 9-11 ms; handheld GPU 6.9 ms;
# 0 of 64 frames late on screen. The first run's opening cutscene held 40 fps while its pipelines were made for the first time (p90 work 15.4 ms); later runs have them cached.
# Audio: the 8 underruns at startup all come before the game's first sound, none in play.
# A 20-minute soak at the start of Cap Kingdom (walking, turning the camera, throwing the cap): one process throughout, frame time p50 16.5 ms, 0 frames dropped on screen
# (4 of 40,200 shown a vsync late), footprint 1.5 GB flat.
# Motion: shaking the device throws the cap (the front end's accelerometer sets DM_BTN_SHAKE, the six-axis sensor in hle_hid.c shakes; the game's "shake the Pro Controller to throw"):
# a DM_CTL Shake threw it, and with DM_SHAKE_G lowered to the still tablet's noise the accelerometer alone made Mario spin-throw.
# Under a spin throw the ground shows a patch of alternate dark pixel columns (an ordered-dither shadow of the half-transparent spin, as the game dithers its transparency); Mario's own
# shadow, standing or in the air, is solid. Not compared with a Switch frame of the same throw.
# The one red log line: "SetRenderEnableConditional: the host draws anyway". The game draws about 16 draws a frame under "draw if not equal" conditions on its
# occlusion reports (agl, Cap Kingdom); evaluating them from real occlusion counts, or skipping them, changed nothing visible (2026-10-31), so render_cond stays off.
# Issue #42 (2026-10-31/11-01, Y700, Cap Kingdom at the wake-up field and the hat tower): the moon's glow flashed for single frames while the camera turned (3-10 of
# 780 frames): the bloom's first pass bound a sampler ID the game registered again before submitting (core: samplers as bound, DM_NVN_SAMP_SNAP), 0 in 2,300 frames
# since. agl's full-screen passes draw past their vertex streams (core: DM_VK_VBOUND). The ground fog parted around a standing Mario and only slowly around a walking
# one: its wave surface (al::FluidSimulateWave) ends in linear render targets (128x128 RGBA16F, 256x128 R32F) that the game's CPU reads from memory, and the host
# left what the GPU drew in the Vulkan images (core: copied back, DM_VK_LIN_BACK). Checked by the user on the tablet 2026-11-01: the fog clears around Mario on contact.
# First-use stalls (2026-11-01, user's route with empty pipeline caches: cap throws at barrels and fences, the first swim, the frog capture): each new pipeline cost 20-35 ms
# (compute 45-105 ms) on the replay thread, 40-30 fps for a moment. Core: new pipelines built in the background (DM_VK_ASYNC_PIPE), every compute shader made ahead;
# cap throws 6 frames over 50 ms -> 0. The first frog capture still builds 33 pipelines at once (new full-screen targets, two 300 ms frames); after a restart the
# saved list prewarms them: 0 pipelines on the replay thread, no drop (user-checked), and the Resume load 4.9 s -> 0.2 s.
# Draws left out while a pipeline builds must reach only targets drawn every frame: looser rules lost the fog for a whole run in 2 of 4 clean starts (the wave
# solver's linear targets, an image kept from the title and drawn once at the load); with the final rule 4 of 4 clean starts matched a run without background builds.
